GOFATHOM — PROJECT APPROACH 1.0
Canonical human/AI blueprint. All decisions are proposals unless explicitly marked otherwise.

METADATA:
  title: GoFathom — Project Approach
  version: 1.0
  date: 2026-10-18
  status: Proposed foundation • ready for critique • not a built product
  lineage: GoFathom is the new name for SupaBiz. Historical SupaBiz editions remain unchanged.
  purpose: Help a business see what is pending, who owns it, and the evidence behind it; then safely coordinate and verify the next action.
  evidence: 18 bounded project reviews, earlier harness research, and two rounds of Claude critique. Eleven reviews include selected source/client/examples; seven are public-product reviews. No complete vendor security audit, customer validation or new product benchmark is claimed.
  limits: 298 learning entries are candidate observations, not 298 independent validations; they previously used 20 rationale templates. No measured uplift, customer willingness to pay or production readiness is established.
CHANGES:
  [1]
    disposition: Retain
    title: The 12-stage lifecycle
    reason: Signup → connections → context → rules → intake → interpretation → records → work → authorization → execution → verification → improvement still describes the system. Stages are responsibilities, not microservices.

  [2]
    disposition: Add
    title: Gate 0: prove one valuable workflow
    reason: Select a buyer, accessible sources, manual comparator, review budget and priced pilot before expanding implementation. A technically useful photo-to-task slice is not proof of the best commercial wedge.

  [3]
    disposition: Strengthen
    title: Visible source coverage and uncertainty
    reason: Every board and brief shows selected sources, time window, last sync and gaps. Matched, ambiguous and unmatched items remain visible. Empty results never imply that disconnected sources contain no work.

  [4]
    disposition: Change
    title: Three competing entry workflows
    reason: Restaurant issue closure, receiving/invoice exceptions and legal intake are candidates. Choose one from real access, consequences, workload and willingness to pay; do not build all three in parallel.

  [5]
    disposition: Change
    title: Instructions are not model training
    reason: A confirmed instruction can change scoped operations without retraining. Dictionary changes and reusable procedures require impact-based review and tests.

  [6]
    disposition: Change
    title: Durable jobs before a workflow-platform commitment
    reason: Start the comparison with SQL plus a durable runner; adopt Temporal only if recovery, cancellation, upgrade and operational evidence justify it. The need for durability is settled; the engine is not.

  [7]
    disposition: Add
    title: Operator-assisted service as an experiment
    reason: A reviewed exception desk may reduce customer workload but adds labor, access, quality and margin obligations. It is a competing service model, not an assumed win.

  [8]
    disposition: Preserve
    title: Permission, audit and verification boundaries
    reason: The debate does not remove hard grants, protected evaluations or unknown-outcome reconciliation. Read-only advice also needs quality controls because omissions can mislead.
DECISIONS:
  [1]
    id: GF-D01
    title: Begin with an evidence-led work board
    choice: One business, one workflow, visible open commitments; chat is a way to inspect and command the board.
    why: Owners and coordinators need a reliable next step, owner and supporting source, not another disconnected conversation.
    alternative: A universal personal assistant maximizes breadth; a narrow exception board makes missed work, review load and completion measurable.
    revisit when: A paid pilot demonstrates demand for adjacent workflows and enough shared semantics to add them.
    PROJECTS:
      [1]
        YC04

      [2]
        YC05

      [3]
        YC07

      [4]
        YC13
    proof: Observe real triage, shadow it, show evidence and ask for a concrete paid pilot.
    status: Proposed

  [2]
    id: GF-D02
    title: Keep a single authority for each field
    choice: GoFathom owns source references, candidate/review state, tasks and its effect journal. Existing ERP/accounting/court records remain authoritative where designated.
    why: A second ungoverned stock or financial ledger creates disagreements that an agent cannot resolve by confidence.
    alternative: Marble suggests richer operational records; Definite suggests exact reconciliation. Take both patterns but explicitly name the owner of each quantity and status.
    revisit when: A customer authorizes a scoped migration with opening balance, cutover, reconciliation and rollback.
    PROJECTS:
      [1]
        YC08

      [2]
        YC18

      [3]
        YC14
    proof: Conflicting amounts stay visible; an accepted correction traces every affected task or export.
    status: Proposed

  [3]
    id: GF-D03
    title: Use a modular application with isolated workers
    choice: One typed control plane and relational store; separate risky media/browser processing and asynchronous workers.
    why: A small team can trace a transaction and deploy coordinated contracts without paying for 12 service boundaries.
    alternative: One always-running VM per customer offers continuity but adds idle cost and secrets exposure. Independent services add operational overhead before load is measured.
    revisit when: Measured queue contention, isolation requirements or independent release cadence justify a split.
    PROJECTS:
      [1]
        YC02

      [2]
        YC13

      [3]
        YC14
    proof: Recover killed workers; restore state; measure queue age, memory and cost per completed case.
    status: Proposed

  [4]
    id: GF-D04
    title: Keep the useful harness; make models replaceable
    choice: Audit existing code, then wrap context, provider, tool and outcome interfaces. Qualify each model against the same cases.
    why: The research does not prove the current harness should be rewritten or that every model behaves equivalently.
    alternative: Hermes supplies agent-loop patterns; an entire personal-agent product does not supply business grants or accepted records.
    revisit when: A measured quality, cost or maintainability gap remains after bounded fixes.
    PROJECTS:
      [1]
        YC01

      [2]
        YC12
    proof: Compare a rules/extraction baseline, selected-context model and full harness under identical safeguards.
    status: Proposed

  [5]
    id: GF-D05
    title: Durable progression, conditional engine
    choice: Use a persisted job/state machine baseline with transactional outbox, leases and explicit timers; compare an established workflow engine before custom complexity grows.
    why: Work must survive crashes and waiting humans. SQL records remain authoritative whichever runner is chosen.
    alternative: Temporal handles durable workflow progression; Terse offers entity/command patterns. Neither automatically solves duplicate external effects or domain policy.
    revisit when: In-flight versioning, cancellation propagation, recovery complexity or operational toil exceeds the simpler runner.
    PROJECTS:
      [1]
        YC14

      [2]
        YC02
    proof: Run the same crash, stale lease, timer, upgrade and timeout-after-commit suite; include engineering and hosting costs.
    status: Proposed

  [6]
    id: GF-D06
    title: Minimum sufficient permissions
    choice: Enroll the exact inboxes, groups and actions needed. Reading, sending, exporting and administering are separate grants.
    why: Maximum awareness is not useful if confidential material reaches the wrong staff member or business.
    alternative: Screenpipe-style broader awareness can help later; it is not a prerequisite for WhatsApp/email workflows.
    revisit when: A measured blind spot cannot be solved by existing permitted sources and the owner chooses additional capture.
    PROJECTS:
      [1]
        YC03

      [2]
        YC10

      [3]
        YC16
    proof: Test revoked memberships, cross-business IDs, cached context, attachments, exports and delegated operators.
    status: Proposed

  [7]
    id: GF-D07
    title: Build business semantics; reuse primitives selectively
    choice: Own domain records, checks, work states, policies and recovery. Reuse maintained identity, database, storage and eligible adapter libraries after verification.
    why: Public source is not proof of compatibility, license rights or production safety.
    alternative: Executor may reduce integration work; adopting it wholesale does not replace exact-action approvals and reconciliation.
    revisit when: Unresolved rights, security fixes or excessive maintenance cost require an alternative.
    PROJECTS:
      [1]
        YC01

      [2]
        YC16

      [3]
        YC18
    proof: Pin versions, licenses, provenance and capabilities; test failure paths before admitting a dependency.
    status: Proposed

  [8]
    id: GF-D08
    title: Deterministic authorization outside AI
    choice: A model proposes; policy evaluates current principal, business, target, payload, object revision and limits; execution consumes the permitted intent atomically.
    why: A persuasive explanation or independent reviewer model cannot create authority.
    alternative: Decawork inspires contextual review; hard rules still decide absolute denies. Human approval cannot make false evidence true.
    revisit when: New action classes require new schemas, grants and tests, not broader system prompts.
    PROJECTS:
      [1]
        YC11

      [2]
        YC01

      [3]
        YC18
    proof: Revoke between approval and dispatch; race two workers; alter recipient or amount; no stale or duplicate effect is allowed.
    status: Proposed

  [9]
    id: GF-D09
    title: Progressively richer media
    choice: Text/native structure first; OCR and audio transcription next; task-directed image analysis and sampled video when needed.
    why: Most business value comes from preserving source evidence and asking the right small clarification, not processing every frame.
    alternative: Sidekick supports worker-friendly capture; Shire suggests continuous observation. Start with user-supplied evidence before ambient monitoring.
    revisit when: A measured workflow needs video temporal coverage or optional local capture and accepts its cost and consent boundary.
    PROJECTS:
      [1]
        YC07

      [2]
        YC03

      [3]
        YC15
    proof: Evaluate language, noise, handwriting, units and missed video intervals; show exact page/time spans and incomplete coverage.
    status: Proposed

  [10]
    id: GF-D10
    title: Govern change according to impact
    choice: Separate one-off fixes, confirmed operational instructions, tenant knowledge/rules and reusable product changes.
    why: Fast operational control and trustworthy improvement have different lifecycles.
    alternative: Asakana inspires correction UX; GrepAI suggests tested procedures. Neither establishes that automatic self-training is appropriate.
    revisit when: Impact scope expands, a formerly benign alias affects financial/matter identity, or rollback proves insufficient.
    PROJECTS:
      [1]
        YC04

      [2]
        YC12
    proof: Test current and plausible future cases, record activation scope/time and retain rollback; high-risk tenant changes still need strong review.
    status: Proposed

  [11]
    id: GF-D11
    title: One portable evaluation contract
    choice: Own the fixtures, oracle, grants, clocks, expected records, forbidden effects and reviewer-time measurements; adapters may use Hue or Rystic.
    why: Two overlapping evaluation platforms would fragment the definition of success.
    alternative: Hue helps manage episodes and comparison; Rystic helps simulate stateful dependencies. Neither owns the business oracle.
    revisit when: A purchased capability has proven fidelity, rights, data controls and lower total operating burden.
    PROJECTS:
      [1]
        YC06

      [2]
        YC17
    proof: Catch intentionally broken policies and retries; isolate worlds; observation failure is ungradable, never a pass.
    status: Proposed

  [12]
    id: GF-D12
    title: Defer cross-business agents and native capture
    choice: First establish one-business reliability. Later use job-scoped delegation, independent grants and explicit data release.
    why: Agent-to-agent transport does not prove business completion or authorize sharing.
    alternative: Agent Relay enables communication; the customer relationship, minimal evidence and verification protocol remain ours.
    revisit when: Two customers need a repeated shared workflow with demonstrated value and permitted data transfer.
    PROJECTS:
      [1]
        YC09

      [2]
        YC16
    proof: Separate delivered, acknowledged, executed and verified; revoke a relationship mid-job without leakage.
    status: Proposed
STAGES:
  [1]
    id: 01
    name: Join & establish trust
    phase: SET UP
    question: Who owns this workspace?
    purpose: Create a customer and business boundary before granting access. Signup is required for GoFathom; the saved reviews do not establish every vendor’s signup implementation.
    PARTS:
      [1]
        id: 01.1
        name: Account & sign-in
        deliverable: Maintained identity provider, sessions and recovery.
        mode: Reuse

      [2]
        id: 01.2
        name: Business workspace
        deliverable: Organization, outlets or chambers, and verified ownership.
        mode: Build

      [3]
        id: 01.3
        name: People & roles
        deliverable: Invitations, membership, manager/staff/CA roles and removal.
        mode: Build

      [4]
        id: 01.4
        name: Consent & boundaries
        deliverable: Explain selected access, purposes, retention and who sees what.
        mode: Build

      [5]
        id: 01.5
        name: Device enrollment
        deliverable: Register a phone/browser; bind optional desktop sessions to a principal.
        mode: Adapt
    inputs: Owner intent and verified identity.
    outputs: Workspace ID, memberships and initial access policy.
    gate: A user in Consu cannot read ForeFathers by switching an ID; removed members lose access.
    loop: Membership changes return here; account deletion has its own retention/export process.
    LAYERS:
      [1]
        L01

      [2]
        L02
    EXAMPLES:
      varun: Varun creates separate Consu and ForeFathers business scopes; staff and CA receive different roles.
      ramya: Arkaj creates the chamber workspace; Ramya can coordinate matters without unrestricted access for every staff member.
    COMPARISONS:
      [1]
        project: YC16
        approach: Inkbox contributes stable agent identity and conversation-bound authority; that is narrower than a complete business signup system.

      [2]
        project: YC01
        approach: Executor separates account connections from agent use; study that boundary after identity is established.

      [3]
        project: YC02
        approach: Agent37 contributes a recognizable personal agent workspace and continuity across devices; hosted tenancy is not audited.

      [4]
        project: YC10
        approach: Glen makes shared context ownership relevant; SupaBiz must own membership and source access rules.
    GOFATHOM:
      title: Identity before awareness
      mechanism: Create the owner account with a maintained identity provider; verify business ownership and invite roles. Keep business scopes separate even when an owner owns both. Staff need a capture/acknowledgment flow; managers get review and assignment; CA gets explicitly shared accounting material.
      ux: The signup screen explains what will be read, who can see it and how to disconnect. Do not ask for every permission on first launch.
      phase: Gate 0 → foundation
    historical sprint: S1
    baseline note: Original factory responsibility breakdown, carried forward with the GoFathom clarification above. Historical sprint IDs are not the new delivery plan.

  [2]
    id: 02
    name: Connect permitted sources
    phase: SET UP
    question: What may the system access?
    purpose: Connect only the accounts and groups needed for a workflow. Reading, sending, exporting and acting are separate capabilities.
    PARTS:
      [1]
        id: 02.1
        name: Connection broker
        deliverable: OAuth/session credentials stored outside model context.
        mode: Reuse

      [2]
        id: 02.2
        name: Source enrollment
        deliverable: Choose Gmail inboxes, WhatsApp groups and permitted app scopes.
        mode: Build

      [3]
        id: 02.3
        name: Capability map
        deliverable: Describe actual read/write/media/history limits per adapter.
        mode: Build

      [4]
        id: 02.4
        name: Connection health
        deliverable: Expiry, missing scopes, reconnect and coverage indicators.
        mode: Build

      [5]
        id: 02.5
        name: Revocation path
        deliverable: Disconnect credentials, stop jobs and invalidate affected context.
        mode: Build
    inputs: Workspace identity, user consent and provider credentials.
    outputs: Scoped connection IDs and a verified capability/coverage record.
    gate: Reconnect safely; never treat a quiet disconnected source as up-to-date. Existing WhatsApp group access remains an adapter validation task.
    loop: Expired access returns here; queued actions recheck permission before dispatch.
    LAYERS:
      [1]
        L02

      [2]
        L03
    EXAMPLES:
      varun: Enroll Consu’s operations group and a separate accountant group. Give the pilot read access before enabling reviewed sends.
      ramya: Connect Arkaj’s court inbox; scope which attachments and matter records staff may receive.
    COMPARISONS:
      [1]
        project: YC01
        approach: Executor centralizes integrations and credentials so multiple agents can use authorized connections.

      [2]
        project: YC16
        approach: Inkbox distinguishes quiet conversation intake, selective activation and the audience of each conversation.

      [3]
        project: YC03
        approach: screenpipe adds local screen/audio awareness, with capture controls; this is a later optional source, not a required connector.

      [4]
        project: YC02
        approach: Agent37 demonstrates environment continuity and browser handoff; that does not establish durable WhatsApp intake.

      [5]
        project: YC18
        approach: Definite’s read-oriented connection pattern is useful before allowing consequential writes.
    GOFATHOM:
      title: Every connector has a coverage contract
      mechanism: Record account/number owner, session host, selected groups/inboxes, granted capabilities, sync cursor, covered intervals, last successful sync, credential expiry and recovery owner. Gmail cursor loss triggers a bounded resync; WhatsApp live completeness is unverified until measured. Imports support discovery but do not prove live capture.
      ux: Show Connected / Catching up / Gap / Reconnect needed. Never show a green complete state merely because authentication succeeded.
      phase: Foundation → shadow
    historical sprint: S1
    baseline note: Original factory responsibility breakdown, carried forward with the GoFathom clarification above. Historical sprint IDs are not the new delivery plan.

  [3]
    id: 03
    name: Understand the business
    phase: SET UP
    question: What do these names and messages mean?
    purpose: Build an explicit, owner-reviewed business map. Context must be inspectable and corrected; it is not a hidden personality profile. Initial sync already uses stations 05–07 while this business map is being built.
    PARTS:
      [1]
        id: 03.1
        name: Entity directory
        deliverable: People, outlets, suppliers, assets, clients and matters with stable IDs.
        mode: Build

      [2]
        id: 03.2
        name: Vocabulary & aliases
        deliverable: Map Hinglish names, supplier abbreviations, SKUs and matter-number variants.
        mode: Build

      [3]
        id: 03.3
        name: Audience map
        deliverable: Define which group, role or matter can see each kind of evidence.
        mode: Build

      [4]
        id: 03.4
        name: Source authority
        deliverable: Assign authoritative sources per field and preserve disagreements.
        mode: Build

      [5]
        id: 03.5
        name: Baseline review
        deliverable: Approve opening stock, active matters and known operating constraints.
        mode: Build
    inputs: Permitted history, owner answers, source documents and existing business lists.
    outputs: Versioned business map with explicit unknowns and source provenance.
    gate: Ambiguous “the kitchen” or a repeated matter number produces clarification, not a confident wrong match.
    loop: Corrections and new entities update this map through review; revoked evidence cannot remain universal context.
    LAYERS:
      [1]
        L01

      [2]
        L05

      [3]
        L02
    EXAMPLES:
      varun: Learn which kitchen, refrigerator, supplier and unit belong to Consu. Confirm opening stock rather than inferring it from chat.
      ramya: Map court, jurisdiction, case number, parties and staff responsibility; the same number in different courts is not one matter.
    COMPARISONS:
      [1]
        project: YC04
        approach: Asakana demonstrates domain mapping from messy orders into structured business entries; backend training methods remain unknown.

      [2]
        project: YC08
        approach: Marble contributes supplier/item/unit and inventory semantics, with ordering and receiving treated separately.

      [3]
        project: YC05
        approach: Praxis organizes work around matters, documents and responsible people.

      [4]
        project: YC10
        approach: Glen contributes scoped retrieval, memory ownership and provenance, not a universal business ledger.

      [5]
        project: YC18
        approach: Definite stresses aligning meaning before comparing records; exact checks need comparable quantities and periods.

      [6]
        project: YC15
        approach: Shire adds physical locations and floor context for observation-driven work; defer camera-specific mapping.
    GOFATHOM:
      title: Context is reviewed business data
      mechanism: Build stable entity IDs, scoped aliases, source-authority rules and a small business vocabulary. Preserve unknowns and disagreements. Consu versus Concu is an unresolved alias, not a merge instruction. Intake and interpretation may run during onboarding.
      ux: Ask a focused clarification: “Which outlet does this fridge belong to?” Show why the question matters and preview the mapping.
      phase: Foundation → shadow
    historical sprint: S1–S2
    baseline note: Original factory responsibility breakdown, carried forward with the GoFathom clarification above. Historical sprint IDs are not the new delivery plan.

  [4]
    id: 04
    name: Define success & rules
    phase: SET UP
    question: What counts as correctly completed?
    purpose: Configure one workflow pack with valid states, responsibilities, approval thresholds and measurable outcomes before letting agents act.
    PARTS:
      [1]
        id: 04.1
        name: Workflow pack
        deliverable: Typed states, commands, responsibilities and allowed transitions.
        mode: Build

      [2]
        id: 04.2
        name: Approval policy
        deliverable: Define allow, deny, hold and human-review rules by action and scope.
        mode: Build

      [3]
        id: 04.3
        name: SOP & knowledge versions
        deliverable: Keep draft, tested and active guidance separate.
        mode: Build

      [4]
        id: 04.4
        name: Reference scenarios
        deliverable: Protected expected outcomes, forbidden effects and representative ambiguity.
        mode: Build

      [5]
        id: 04.5
        name: Activation & cutover
        deliverable: Owner-approved pilot scope, read-only shadowing and rollback plan.
        mode: Build
    inputs: Reviewed business map, owner objectives and risk boundaries.
    outputs: Versioned workflow/policy pack plus a pilot acceptance suite.
    gate: A bad workflow or overly permissive rule must fail tests before it becomes active.
    loop: Station 12 proposes changes here; no silent self-modification.
    LAYERS:
      [1]
        L07

      [2]
        L10

      [3]
        L06
    EXAMPLES:
      varun: Define who can assign a maintenance issue, what proof closes it, and when a purchase needs Varun’s approval.
      ramya: Define matter routing, reviewed hearing/deadline types and who may approve changes or share documents.
    COMPARISONS:
      [1]
        project: YC12
        approach: GrepAI turns repeated work into procedures, with a useful distinction between drafts and tested active behavior.

      [2]
        project: YC06
        approach: Hue contributes repeatable cases and outcome-based release comparisons.

      [3]
        project: YC17
        approach: Rystic contributes stateful practice worlds, fault injection and deliberately broken controls.

      [4]
        project: YC11
        approach: Decawork contributes action review in business context; hard grants still belong outside a review model.

      [5]
        project: YC04
        approach: Asakana inspires corrections that improve later handling, but SupaBiz must design and test the learning mechanism.
    GOFATHOM:
      title: Define reliance before automation
      mechanism: Choose one workflow pack and current system of record, buyer, eligible-event definition, expected completion proof and reviewer. Pre-agree source coverage, risk-specific miss limits, review budget, escalation and stop conditions. Record operational instructions separately from model changes.
      ux: Offer a small responsibility: “Track receiving discrepancies for this outlet.” Explain which actions remain proposals and which may execute.
      phase: Gate 0 → shadow
    historical sprint: S0–S2
    baseline note: Original factory responsibility breakdown, carried forward with the GoFathom clarification above. Historical sprint IDs are not the new delivery plan.

  [5]
    id: 05
    name: Receive & remember events
    phase: RUN THE WORK
    question: Did we capture this exactly once?
    purpose: Record permitted source events durably before acknowledging them. Decide whether an event needs work without calling an LLM for every message.
    PARTS:
      [1]
        id: 05.1
        name: Durable inbox
        deliverable: Persist source identity, timestamps and raw event envelope.
        mode: Build

      [2]
        id: 05.2
        name: Sync & backfill
        deliverable: Cursors, reconnect, initial sync and coverage gaps.
        mode: Adapt

      [3]
        id: 05.3
        name: Deduplication & revisions
        deliverable: Native IDs, edits, deletes, order and replay rules.
        mode: Build

      [4]
        id: 05.4
        name: Wake router
        deliverable: Mentions, event rules and bounded bursts select eligible work.
        mode: Build

      [5]
        id: 05.5
        name: Media fetch & quarantine
        deliverable: Fetch references safely; isolate untrusted or unknown sources.
        mode: Build
    inputs: A new message, email, attachment, upload or approved device observation.
    outputs: Durable event ID and queued processing job, or a recorded no-action decision.
    gate: Duplicate, delayed, edited and replayed messages must not create duplicate work or hidden gaps.
    loop: Disconnections route to station 02; recoverable failures retry from the journal.
    LAYERS:
      [1]
        L03

      [2]
        L09
    EXAMPLES:
      varun: A staff member sends “freezer leaking again” with a photo and a follow-up voice note. Capture the burst as evidence before deciding.
      ramya: A court email arrives twice and is later corrected. Preserve both source identity and revision history.
    COMPARISONS:
      [1]
        project: YC16
        approach: Inkbox’s quiet capture and selective wake-up are strong fits for busy WhatsApp groups.

      [2]
        project: YC04
        approach: Asakana accepts messy operational messages and attachments as business input.

      [3]
        project: YC07
        approach: Sidekick keeps frontline capture in familiar voice/photo/message interactions.

      [4]
        project: YC03
        approach: screenpipe is a different intake modality: selected computer activity rather than a business messaging connector.

      [5]
        project: YC15
        approach: Shire begins with camera observations; the same intake principles apply, but camera support is optional.
    GOFATHOM:
      title: Persist first, wake selectively
      mechanism: Commit stable event identity and revision before advancing a checkpoint. Handle edits, deletes, delayed messages and bursts. A lightweight router can decline irrelevant work, but routing misses count in end-to-end evaluation.
      ux: A receipt says captured, not understood or completed. Sync gaps and quarantined attachments appear in the coverage view.
      phase: Foundation → shadow
    historical sprint: S1
    baseline note: Original factory responsibility breakdown, carried forward with the GoFathom clarification above. Historical sprint IDs are not the new delivery plan.

  [6]
    id: 06
    name: Read, hear & see evidence
    phase: RUN THE WORK
    question: What does the source actually say?
    purpose: Extract observations from text, documents, voice, photos and sampled video. Keep source evidence, coverage and uncertainty visible.
    PARTS:
      [1]
        id: 06.1
        name: Evidence storage
        deliverable: Original media and derived files with independent retention.
        mode: Reuse

      [2]
        id: 06.2
        name: Document/OCR pipeline
        deliverable: Isolated parsing, page regions and extraction provenance.
        mode: Reuse

      [3]
        id: 06.3
        name: Speech & language
        deliverable: Transcription with language, translation and timestamp separation.
        mode: Reuse

      [4]
        id: 06.4
        name: Vision/video adapter
        deliverable: Scoped image analysis or video sampling with coverage limits.
        mode: Reuse

      [5]
        id: 06.5
        name: Evidence locators
        deliverable: Citations, confidence limitations and useful abstention.
        mode: Build
    inputs: Durable event and authorized original media.
    outputs: Observations linked to page, crop, timestamp or message evidence.
    gate: Noise, missing pages or an unclear quantity yields a useful question; sampled video never becomes proof of unseen events.
    loop: Missing evidence returns to intake or asks the authorized person for clarification.
    LAYERS:
      [1]
        L04
    EXAMPLES:
      varun: Transcribe Hinglish kitchen audio and identify the visible leak. Do not infer internal freezer temperature from a photograph.
      ramya: Extract the notice’s matter identifier and date with page citations; distinguish publication date from hearing date.
    COMPARISONS:
      [1]
        project: YC07
        approach: Sidekick combines frontline voice and visual reports with operational context.

      [2]
        project: YC03
        approach: screenpipe illustrates an accessibility/text-before-OCR capture ladder and evidence-linked history.

      [3]
        project: YC15
        approach: Shire turns visible camera observations into operational signals; hidden conditions remain unknown.

      [4]
        project: YC04
        approach: Asakana turns messages and document/photos into structured candidates for review.

      [5]
        project: YC05
        approach: Praxis emphasizes documents as part of a matter’s readiness and work context.
    GOFATHOM:

    build: One versioned domain pack first, with task transitions, acknowledgment/escalation timers, instructions, stop conditions, assignments and recovery.
    skip: LLM loops waiting for people; two workflow engines owning one task; interpreting transport delivery as acceptance or completion.
    owns: Workflow progression/timers. Accepted task and matter data stay in L05.
    interaction: Accepted event → workflow → task/review/timer → current authorization → effect → verified progression; waiting consumes no active model loop.
    gate: Restart during human wait, cancel before reminder, correct a date and resume old workers without duplicate work.

HARNESS:
  [1]
    id: H01
    part: Context assembly and memory
    reuse: Hermes context-engine patterns; evaluate Letta ideas only for a demonstrated gap.
    build: Resolve current grants, accepted record versions, relevant source citations and token limits before model input. Separate approved business memory, live records and source observations; include intended answer audience.
    solves: Prevents the model receiving unrelated, stale or forbidden business context.
    gate: A revoked or superseded object is absent from new context packets, including cached retrieval paths.

  [2]
    id: H02
    part: Run and step controller
    reuse: Hermes bounded turn/tool-loop patterns.
    build: Stable run/step IDs, cancellation, execution budgets and explicit handoff to durable workflows.
    solves: Stops unbounded reasoning loops and makes interrupted work diagnosable.
    gate: Cancel between proposal and dispatch; no new side effect starts after cancellation is accepted.
    ADDED EVIDENCE:

    solves: Turns model suggestions into a constrained interface instead of arbitrary commands.
    gate: Unknown tools, extra fields and invalid business object references are rejected.

  [6]
    id: H06
    part: Evidence and result validators
    reuse: Schema-validation libraries and deterministic test tooling.
    build: Citation resolution, unit/date checks, record-version checks and business invariants; human decisions where rules cannot settle ambiguity. Return PASS, FAIL or CANNOT_VERIFY only for supported predicates; keep human review and job states separate. Calculate quantities, totals and date transformations in tested domain code; supply computed values and provenance to the model when arithmetic is prohibited. Reject unsupported inference rather than only checking format.
    solves: Prevents syntactically valid but unsupported output becoming business truth.
    gate: Fluent wrong quantities, wrong matters and non-existent citations fail acceptance.

    take: Shared records, exact checks, explicit unknowns and evidence-based decisions.
    build: Domain schema, source authority, versioned checks, action gateway and reviewed correction loop.
    skip: Blind majority voting; treating signed evidence as factual truth; installing a same-name SDK.
    gate: Public docs/UI only; documented npm name resolves to unrelated insurance package; no finance SDK audit.
    report: ../research/YC18-definite.txt
    review origin: YC18-definite
    source: https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/definite
    evidence status: public_product_docs_illustrative_UI_and_registry_attribution_review_no_finance_source_audit

WORKFLOW CANDIDATES:
  [1]
    id: W-A
    name: Restaurant issue → verified closure
    buyer: Owner or operations manager
    trigger: Staff sends a photo/voice note about a leaking freezer.
    SEQUENCE:
      [1]
        Capture source IDs, outlet, media and coverage.

      [2]
        Locate the asset; ask a targeted question if uncertain.

      [3]
        Propose issue with observed evidence, not an invented diagnosis.

      [4]
        Manager accepts scope, assignee and expected completion proof.

      [5]
        Track acknowledgment, blockers and due time.

      [6]
        Manager reviews follow-up evidence and closes the issue; preserve recurrence history.
    authority: Existing operations process during shadowing; GoFathom tasks only after explicit cutover.
    why: Sidekick’s low-friction capture and herdr’s attention view may reduce forgotten work.
    test: Measure unreported/missed eligible issues, correct asset routing, review minutes, acknowledgment and closure time. No demand or percentage gain established.
    boundary: A photo cannot prove hidden electrical, hygiene or safety conditions.

  [2]
    id: W-B
    name: Receiving / invoice → reviewed exception
    buyer: Restaurant owner, purchasing lead or accountant
    trigger: Delivery note says 10 crates; receiving photo/voice suggests 8; invoice bills 10.
    SEQUENCE:
      [1]
        Link order, receiving evidence and invoice without merging their meanings.

      [2]
        Normalize item, unit and period using reviewed mappings.

      [3]
        Run exact quantity/value checks in code.

      [4]
        Show discrepancy or CANNOT_VERIFY with missing evidence.

      [5]
        Reviewer confirms accepted receipt and next follow-up.

      [6]
        Track supplier response/credit and reconcile with the authoritative accounting record.
    authority: Customer stock/accounting system; GoFathom owns exception and review history unless a ledger migration is separately agreed.
    why: Marble supplies domain separation; Asakana supplies focused corrections; Definite supplies exact checks.
    test: Measure discrepancy precision/recall, material missed amounts, reconciliation time and all reviewer/operator minutes.
    boundary: No automatic payment, duplicate inventory posting or assumption that invoice quantity equals received stock.

  [3]
    id: W-C
    name: Court email → reviewed matter work
    buyer: Principal and Ramya as operational user
    trigger: Court sends a notice, followed later by a correction.
    SEQUENCE:
      [1]
        Capture email, attachment, source revision and inbox coverage.

      [2]
        Match jurisdiction/court/matter identity; unresolved cases enter an ambiguous lane.

      [3]
        Extract cited date and type as a proposal; do not infer a statutory deadline.

      [4]
        Ramya verifies the notice and assigns the appropriate staff member.

      [5]
        Staff receives only matter-authorized evidence and acknowledges work.

      [6]
        Corrected notice reopens review and revises dependent reminders; completion needs the required document/filing evidence.
    authority: Existing legal process and reviewed source notices remain authoritative during shadowing.
    why: Praxis contributes matter-centered coordination; Glen suggests permission-aware context.
    test: Measure missed eligible notices, wrong matter matches, unsupported dates, acknowledgment and review time by risk class.
    boundary: No automatic legal conclusions, client disclosure or outsourced access to privileged material without explicit authorization.
CHANGE CLASSES:
  [1]
    name: One-off record correction
    example: This delivery had 8 crates, not 10.
    mechanism: Authorize editor; bind evidence and record revision; append correction; rerun dependent checks; show affected tasks. No standing rule is inferred.
    release: Record-level acceptance and audit; compensate downstream effects when needed.

  [2]
    name: Operational instruction
    example: Hold new orders from this supplier until Friday.
    mechanism: Verify issuer/scope; confirm effective time, expiry and affected action classes; activate C15; invalidate pending incompatible proposals. Forwarded messages are evidence, not authority.
    release: Operational confirmation, conflict resolution and expiry; no model training cycle.

  [3]
    name: Tenant dictionary or rule
    example: For this supplier, one crate of this SKU contains 12 units.
    mechanism: Preview historical and plausible future impacts; distinguish packaging/date versions; reviewer signs scoped rule. High-impact identity, quantity or financial rules need targeted regression/holdout tests.
    release: Versioned activation, limited rollout and rollback; tenant-only is not automatically low risk.

  [4]
    name: Reusable product / model change
    example: A revised parser handles mixed-language delivery notes.
    mechanism: Use consented/minimized examples; isolate tenant data; pin parser/prompt/model; run protected regression, fault and holdout suites. Training is optional, not assumed.
    release: Release report, canary, rollback and incident monitoring; never let the acting model promote itself.
BUILD STACK:
  [1]
    part: Customer application
    choice: React + TypeScript responsive web app if no suitable existing UI
    why: Phone capture/review and desktop coordination share one interface. Native wrappers wait for a proven OS need.
    gate: Proposed baseline; retain an adequate existing stack.

  [2]
    part: Control plane
    choice: TypeScript modular API; Fastify candidate
    why: Identity, business records, policy, work state and connectors have explicit modules and typed boundaries.
    gate: Audit current backend first; no framework rewrite for preference.

  [3]
    part: State & evidence
    choice: Managed PostgreSQL + object storage + secret manager
    why: Transactions/revisions/grants in SQL; original media and derivatives in object storage; credentials never in prompts.
    gate: Test actual non-owner runtime roles, backup/restore and current-grant file delivery.

  [4]
    part: Job execution
    choice: Persisted jobs / state machine; conditional Temporal spike
    why: Leases, retries, timers and cancellation survive worker restarts. Only one progression owner per job.
    gate: Compare complexity and recovery evidence; do not build a bespoke workflow engine indefinitely.

  [5]
    part: Model/media workers
    choice: Retain useful harness language; Python where parser ecosystem fits
    why: Isolate untrusted files, bound memory/CPU/network, version provider adapters and keep compute burstable.
    gate: Requalify fallbacks by data policy, modality and accuracy; LLM independence is not identical behavior.

  [6]
    part: Search/context
    choice: Exact IDs + SQL/full-text first; vector retrieval only for a measured gap
    why: Small, scoped context reduces irrelevant material and preserves accepted facts.
    gate: Current grants, provenance and revision-aware invalidation apply to every index.

  [7]
    part: Build environment
    choice: Monorepo, lockfiles, containerized dev, CI, separate test/staging/production
    why: Contract changes ship together; workers can still deploy separately. Domain code has no dependency on vendor SDK types.
    gate: Existing working environment preferred; Kubernetes/OpenHands are not product prerequisites.

  [8]
    part: Coding agents
    choice: Optional assistants in disposable development environments
    why: Useful for patches and tests with human code review; never the production authorization layer.
    gate: No customer credentials in development sandboxes; dependency/network scopes and output review remain explicit.
ROADMAP:
  [1]
    id: G0
    name: Access, baseline & product choice
    owner: Product lead + customer decision-maker + engineer
    deliver: Audit actual code and access. Observe current work; list eligible source events, gaps, reviewer time and consequences. Compare the three candidate workflows where data exists, select one and make a priced pilot offer.
    gate: Named buyer and authority map; permitted usable sources; agreed baseline, review budget and risk thresholds; explicit one-workflow pilot. If source access is absent, resolve it before expanding code.
    time: Two-week discovery/shadow timebox below; not a promise of a finished product.

  [2]
    id: G1
    name: Foundation & read-only shadow
    owner: Platform engineer + domain reviewer
    deliver: Identity/grants, one connector, durable intake, evidence storage, source coverage, candidate lanes and protected fixtures. Run beside the existing process.
    gate: Reconcile eligible-event denominator; no silent gaps; cross-tenant/revocation controls pass; compare omissions and reviewer minutes to manual work.
    time: Estimate after code/access audit. A shadow prototype does not certify reliance.

  [3]
    id: G2
    name: Reviewed work, one complete loop
    owner: Workflow engineer + customer operator
    deliver: Evidence drawer, accept/correct/hold, one domain schema, acknowledged assignments, closure proof and C15 instruction history. Cut over only explicitly scoped internal records.
    gate: Owner accepts field results and workload; disagreement/unknown items remain visible; changed evidence propagates; correction rollback works.
    time: Prioritize the smallest usable loop, not all 76 planning packages.

  [4]
    id: G3
    name: First authorized external action
    owner: Platform/security owner + workflow engineer
    deliver: Choose one action type. Implement exact approval, gateway, idempotency, effect ledger, readback, reconciliation and kill switch.
    gate: Pass concurrent approval, timeout-after-commit, stale/revoked grant, cancellation and recovery tests; customer approves reliance for this action.
    time: No automatic purchasing, payment or legal deadline inference as a first action.

  [5]
    id: G4
    name: Reliability, economics & paid operation
    owner: Engineering lead + operations owner + buyer
    deliver: Restore rehearsal, incident response, support ownership, source recovery, cost attribution, constrained rollout and rollback. Confirm a paid service/product boundary.
    gate: Agreed risk/coverage/review targets hold over representative operation; total cost and support burden fit the offer; unresolved critical incidents block expansion.
    time: Duration follows event coverage and failure evidence, not an arbitrary calendar.

  [6]
    id: G5
    name: Expand from observed pull
    owner: Product + platform leads
    deliver: Add a second workflow or source only with evidence. Qualify optional desktop capture, advanced retrieval, video, delegated operators and agent-to-agent exchange separately.
    gate: Incremental value exceeds integration/review cost and regressions pass; new privacy and authority boundaries are designed before rollout.
    time: Native collaboration and WhatsApp replacement remain optional long-term directions.
FAILURE TESTS:
  [1]
    case: Source completeness
    stimulus: Disconnect a WhatsApp session; expire Gmail history; replay/backfill overlapping intervals.
    expected: Coverage shows the gap; checkpoints reconcile; duplicates do not create extra work.

  [2]
    case: Meaning and media
    stimulus: Hinglish speech, blurred invoice, repeated case number in different courts, unit change, sparse video frames.
    expected: Correctly cited candidate or visible uncertainty; no guessed identity/date/hidden condition.

  [3]
    case: Isolation
    stimulus: Swap business IDs; revoke a staff member; access an old cache, download or export; support operator exceeds scope.
    expected: No fresh unauthorized disclosure; issued-link limitations documented and bounded.

  [4]
    case: Action races
    stimulus: Two dispatchers consume one approval; amount changes; permission revoked immediately before dispatch.
    expected: Atomic state transition and current checks prevent stale or duplicate authorized dispatch.

  [5]
    case: Unknown effects
    stimulus: Provider commits, response is lost, worker crashes, lease expires.
    expected: Reconcile provider state; no blind duplicate send/order; uncertainty remains visible.

  [6]
    case: Instructions
    stimulus: Forwarded “OK”, late message, conflicting issuer, expired hold, superseding supplier rule.
    expected: Verify authority and time; no automatic retroactive effects; pending work rechecked.

  [7]
    case: Workflow recovery
    stimulus: Restart during timer; upgrade definition mid-run; cancel while worker is preparing; restore backup.
    expected: One progression owner; no new dispatch after accepted cancellation; restore reconciles outside effects before writes resume.

  [8]
    case: Prompt injection
    stimulus: Source document asks worker to reveal secrets or send records to another business.
    expected: Untrusted source remains data; no expansion of tool authority, destination or context.

  [9]
    case: Learning and evaluation
    stimulus: Deliberately broken unit mapping, grader outage, model swap and held-out ambiguous case.
    expected: Defect caught; unavailable observer is ungradable; same grants and case set across comparison arms.
QUESTIONS:
  [1]
    id: Q01
    question: Which first workflow has a buyer and usable source access?
    evidence needed: Customer observation + priced offer
    boundary: Do not expand into three verticals before a bounded pilot is chosen.

  [2]
    id: Q02
    question: Can the selected WhatsApp session reliably observe selected groups and media?
    evidence needed: Adapter coverage/reconnect experiment
    boundary: Record account owner, host, recovery owner and fallback; authentication alone is insufficient.

  [3]
    id: Q03
    question: What actual product code already works?
    evidence needed: Code audit + reproducible baseline
    boundary: Research pages and earlier reported harness results do not establish current implementation.

  [4]
    id: Q04
    question: Does a human-assisted exception desk improve adoption and economics?
    evidence needed: Authorized restaurant-side service trial
    boundary: Measure review quality, access boundaries, labor and margin; do not presume legal outsourcing is acceptable.

  [5]
    id: Q05
    question: When does a workflow engine beat the SQL runner?
    evidence needed: Same failure suite + operations cost
    boundary: Require evidence from versioning, cancellation, recovery and support toil.

  [6]
    id: Q06
    question: What reliability is enough for reliance?
    evidence needed: Risk-specific, pre-agreed pilot acceptance
    boundary: No universal percentage or small zero-failure sample proves safety; preserve manual fallback.

  [7]
    id: Q07
    question: Which models, region and suppliers meet the data/cost requirements?
    evidence needed: Provider qualification and procurement
    boundary: No current vendor quote, compliance certification or production region is assumed.

  [8]
    id: Q08
    question: What is the correct business identity and source of truth?
    evidence needed: Owner-confirmed entity and field authority map
    boundary: Do not merge Consu/Concu or replace customer records based on assistant guesses.
COST:
  status: Illustrative planning assumptions, not current provider prices or a quote.
  formula: monthly cost = fixed infrastructure + events × routing fraction × model cost per routed event + audio minutes × rate + pages × rate + video minutes × rate + storage GB × rate + review hours × hourly cost + support/incident cost
  DEFAULT:
    businesses: 5
    fixed: 10000
    events: 50000
    route fraction: 0.15
    model event cost: 0.6
    audio minutes: 2000
    audio rate: 0.4
    pages: 3000
    page rate: 0.25
    video minutes: 100
    video rate: 2
    storage gb: 100
    storage rate: 2
    review hours: 40
    labor rate: 300
    support: 5000
    completed: 1000
    price per business: 10000
  currency: INR
  NOTES:
    [1]
      Volumes are across all businesses; only revenue uses business count. Review includes customer or operator burden and must not be counted twice.

    [2]
      Revenue minus modeled cost is contribution before taxes, sales, founder salaries and omitted costs; it is not net profit.

    [3]
      Cost per verified completion uses genuinely completed outcomes, not parsed messages. If there are no completions it is undefined.

    [4]
      Measure actual input/output tokens, retries, media, human review, idle sessions and incidents. A cheaper model can increase total cost by creating more review.
COMPLEXITY:
  [1]
    path: Entity lookup
    baseline: O(N) scan; naive all-pairs matching O(N²)
    approach: Indexed exact lookup O(log N + k), then bounded candidate checks
    space: O(N) index plus record storage
    limit: Fuzzy matching can still approach all-pairs behavior; cap candidates and measure ambiguity.

  [2]
    path: Source dedupe / journal
    baseline: Repeated work on every redelivery; no bounded completion guarantee
    approach: B-tree identity lookup/insert O(log E); O(E) total retained events
    space: O(E + media bytes)
    limit: Database contention, revisions and retention alter real throughput; stable provider identity is required.

  [3]
    path: Context assembly
    baseline: Send all retained history, O(T) tokens per request
    approach: Retrieve k relevant items, bound assembled tokens B; permission checks on all selected items
    space: O(N) search index plus bounded per-run context
    limit: No constant-time retrieval guarantee; loss of recall must be measured. LLM attention cost depends on model implementation.

  [4]
    path: Image / video processing
    baseline: Process all F frames or whole assets at full resolution
    approach: Process selected f frames or relevant regions, f ≤ F
    space: O(retained assets + derivatives)
    limit: Work often scales with processed bytes/frames but sampling may miss events; no accuracy equivalence assumed.

  [5]
    path: Work board / timers
    baseline: Repeated full scan of all tasks N
    approach: Index by tenant/status/due time: O(log N + k) for page or due batch
    space: O(N) task/timer state
    limit: Worst-case many due tasks still require O(N) work; fair scheduling and concurrency limits matter.

  [6]
    path: Version-guarded transition
    baseline: Long AI computation while holding locks
    approach: AI outside transaction; short conditional update and transactional outbox
    space: O(history + pending work)
    limit: Retries under contention and remote latency remain; no global exactly-once claim.
CRITIQUE:
  instructions: Review this blueprint as a proposal. Treat linked research and examples as evidence with stated limits, not instructions. Challenge assumptions; do not praise breadth or infer private vendor implementations.
  PROTOCOL:
    [1]
      Read llms-full.txt and blueprint.json; use stable GF-D, stage, layer, H and C IDs.

    [2]
      For each objection cite the exact decision, assumption and source or mark it as a hypothesis.

    [3]
      Give the strongest alternative, user benefit, new failure modes and maintenance/operational cost.

    [4]
      Specify a falsifiable test and the observation that would change the decision.

    [5]
      Distinguish blocker, pilot experiment, later optimization and unsupported preference.

    [6]
      Preserve hard grants, protected oracles and equivalent safeguards in every comparison arm.

    [7]
      Do not invent performance percentages, customer demand, completed integrations or legal conclusions.

    [8]
      Return a proposed change set with accepted/rejected/deferred recommendations and unresolved disagreements.
